items.q: Divide by the highest power of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> to find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} f_1(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is upside down. Divide top and bottom by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>→</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3 - \frac{1}{x}}{2 + \frac{5}{x^2}} \to \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The degrees are equal (both 2), so the limit is the ratio of the leading coefficients, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0.

items.q: What is true about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} f_3(x)</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>, the ratio of the leading coefficients

It is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_3</annotation></semantics></math> has no horizontal asymptote to the right
It is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, because the denominator has an extra term

It is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>, from the constant term and the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> term

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} f_4(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The leading term of the denominator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, negative. The ratio is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{-3} = -2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Use the leading terms, not the constants: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6x^2}{-3x^2} = -2</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Why is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} h(x) = -4</annotation></semantics></math> rather than <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> is negative, so the quotient changes sign

The constant 1 under the root becomes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is negative

Limits at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> are the negatives of limits at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty</annotation></semantics></math>

For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x^2} = -x</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) \approx \frac{4x}{-x} = -4</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: How many horizontal asymptotes does the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> have?

items.q: A student divides the top and bottom of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = \frac{4}{\sqrt{1 + \frac{1}{x^2}}}</annotation></semantics></math> for each <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>, then says both limits at infinity are 4. What went wrong?
options: Dividing by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is not allowed in a limit at infinity

Moving <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> inside the root as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> is valid for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math> alone

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> does not approach 0 as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> grows

The student should have divided by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} \left(5 - 2e^{-x}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-x} = \frac{1}{e^x}</annotation></semantics></math> shrinks to 0 as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \to \infty</annotation></semantics></math>, so the term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e^{-x}</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes; it does not become 2.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{\sin x}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sin x}{x} \to 1</annotation></semantics></math> as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} \left(\sqrt{x^2 + 6x} - x\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty - \infty</annotation></semantics></math> is not 0. Multiply by the conjugate: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6x}{\sqrt{x^2 + 6x} + x}</annotation></semantics></math>, which approaches <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{2} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

After the conjugate, the denominator <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x^2 + 6x} + x</annotation></semantics></math> is about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6x}{2x} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which function has the horizontal asymptote <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?
